terms.comment: Classically the pair means “up and down, to and fro”, of movement: nē sūrsum deorsum cursitēs (Ter. Eun. 2.2.47, Lewis & Short s.v. deorsum). Lewis & Short gives no instance of it for things in disorder, Traupman’s sense; there omnia is the subject: “everything was up and down”.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 110.
